utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, good morning to all of you. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-01-47-A, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I would like to begin in the usual way by ensuring that the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Hadzihasanovic, can you hear me in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT HADZIHASANOVIC: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What about all of the counsel?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. We can hear it and understand it. For the Defence of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and our legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. For the Defence of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. It's Antoinette Issa, with me is Julia Thibord, and our case manager Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Good. I want to apologise for bringing you out so early. This is not unusual in this Tribunal. You will understand the limitations imposed on us all by the arrangements. So I would like to call formally for the appearances. Would counsel for Mr. Hadzihasanovic so signify.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the Defence of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that counsel for Mr. Kubura and counsel for the Prosecution are the same?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, as you are aware, Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires that Status Conferences be held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody at intervals no less than 120 days. This is the third Status Conference at the appeals stage in the case of Prosecution against Hadzihasanovic and Kubura. The last Status Conference in this case was held on the 11th December, 2006. This conference, therefore, falls within the 120-day period prescribed by Rule 65 bis. While Mr. Hadzihasanovic is presently in the custody -- in custody at the United Nations Detention Centre, Mr. Kubura was granted early release on 11th April 2006, and therefore he was not strictly entitled to a Status Conference under Rule 65 bis. However, in the interests of justice and in order to facilitate the appeals process, he was invited to be represented at this Status Conference along with his colleague Mr. Hadzihasanovic. I am pleased to see that Mr. Kubura's counsel joined us for this Status Conference. Again, I bid you all a warm welcome. I would like to remind the parties that Status Conferences serve two purposes. First, they allow the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to the appeal and detention conditions; and second, they provide an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. I will begin with the second of these objectives; namely, an update. This case involves three appeals filed by Mr. Hadzihasanovic, Mr. Kubura, and the Prosecution. As you know, the pleadings are now closed. The hearing will be scheduled in due course. I would merely recapitulate the main steps that have occurred so far. On 15 March 2006, Trial Chamber II rendered its judgement in the case of Prosecutor against Hadzihasanovic and Kubura. Mr. Kubura filed his notice of appeal from that judgement on 13th April 2006. Mr. Hadzihasanovic filed his notice of appeal on 18th April 2006, and on the same day the Prosecution filed its notice of appeal. Subsequently, Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura sought extensions of time to file their appeal briefs, pending translations of the trial judgement. The judgement had been rendered in French, a language that Mr. Hadzihasanovic and counsel for Mr. Kubura do not speak. On 27 June 2006, I, as Pre-Appeal Judge, granted Mr. Hadzihasanovic's motion, seeking an extension of time for the submission of his appeal brief until 45 days after the transmission to him of a partial B/C/S translation of the trial judgement with a full translation to be completed subsequently. Mr. Kubura requested an extension corresponding to the full 75-day period ordinarily allowed under Rule 111 for the filing of his appeal brief. He was granted an extension until six days after the transmission to his counsel of a certified English translation of the trial judgement. The decision also found that the Prosecution was entitled to file a consolidated brief and to wait until 40 days after the filing of the second of the two appellants' briefs. Meanwhile, as I have said, the Prosecution filed a notice of appeal on 18th April 2006. It filed its appeal brief on 3 July 2006. Mr. Kubura and Mr. Hadzihasanovic subsequently filed separate motions seeking extensions of time to file their respondents' briefs until 40 days after the transmission of translations of the trial judgement to Mr. Kubura's counsel and to Mr. Hadzihasanovic respectively. The motions were granted on 26th July and 8th August 2006. Both decisions noted that the Prosecution would be permitted to file a consolidated brief within 15 days of the filing of the later of the two response briefs of Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura. The English translation of the full trial judgement was transmitted to the parties on 23 November 2006, and the B/C/S translation or the full trial judgement was transmitted to the parties on 1 December 2006. At the Status Conference held in this case on 11 December 2006, I granted the parties' requests, which were agreed to by counsel for both accused and the Prosecution, to modify the deadlines previously set for the filing of certain pleadings. Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura were granted an extension for the filing of their pre-appeal briefs until 22 January 2007 and for the filing of the response briefs to the Prosecution's appeal until 10 January 2007. The Prosecution was granted an extension of time for the filing of its consolidated brief until 30 January 2007. In accordance with the modified filing deadlines, Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura filed their response briefs in the Prosecution's appeal on 10 January 2007. The Prosecution filed its consolidated reply brief on 30 January 2007. Mr. Kubura filed his appeal brief on 22 January 2007. On 18 January 2007, counsel for Mr. Hadzihasanovic filed a motion seeking an extension of the word limit for Mr. Hadzihasanovic's appeal brief from 30.000 to 39.000 words. In my capacity as Pre-Appeal Judge in this case, I dismissed the motion on 22 January 2007. A day later, the Defence for Mr. Hadzihasanovic sought reconsideration of that decision or, alternatively, an extension of time for filing of its pre-appeal brief. On 30 January 2007, I denied the motion for reconsideration but granted Mr. Hadzihasanovic leave to file his appeal brief within five days of that decision. The decision further confirmed that the Prosecution was entitled to file its consolidated response brief within 40 days of the filing of the later of the two appeal briefs of Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura. Mr. Hadzihasanovic subsequently filed his confidential brief on 5 February 2007, together with annexes amounting to 3200 pages, four DVDs, and two CDs. On 20 February 2007, the Appeals Chamber rendered a decision which declared null and void the appeal briefs filed by Mr. Hadzihasanovic on the ground that they did not comply with paragraph (C) of the Practice Direction on the length of briefs and motions, and the decision of 30 January 2007. It directed the registry to remove the appeal brief annexes from the case file. The Appeals Chamber ordered Mr. Hadzihasanovic, if he so wished, to re-file the annexes to his appeal brief within one week of the date of that decision. Mr. Hadzihasanovic accordingly re-filed his confidential brief annexes on 27 February 2007. On 19 March 2007, the Prosecution filed its confidential consolidated response brief to the appeals of Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura. Mr. Kubura filed his reply brief and Mr. Hadzihasanovic filed his confidential reply brief on 3rd April 2007, that is yesterday. Thus, the briefing in all three appeals is now complete. Now, if I have recapitulated the steps, main steps, correctly, would the parties indicate whether they have any concerns remaining in respect of the appeals.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Judge. May it please the Court. I would just like to make a brief submission regarding one of the appeal grounds which concerns the appeal which was raised by my client, Mr. Hadzihasanovic. On the third ground of appeal, which was of course briefed in the initial appeal responded to, and we replied yesterday, there is an issue of obtaining translations or official translation of an audio-recording. We indicated yesterday in our reply brief that we were in the process of obtaining this official translation of a segment, an audio-recording, a segment from the judgement, and I would just like to indicate to the Pre-Appeals Chamber that we are in the process of obtaining this official translation from CLSS, and that we will submit it to the Appeals Chamber in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, when is it likely to be ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We anticipate any time -- any day, any day, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Perhaps I can hear from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I -- we were not actually aware of this matter until Mr. Bourgon raised it. I would have to, obviously, consider it and have the opportunity to understand exactly what -- what issue this relates to specifically in the reply brief. As you know, it was filed yesterday, and we haven't had that much time to consider our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, I understand you, Mr. Bourgon; you're merely conveying the information to the Court and not to be making a complaint?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, not a complaint at all. Simply to indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- the issue -- maybe I can clarify the issue for the Appeals Chamber. In our appeal, one of the -- one of the arguments that we raised was that there was a problem with the official translation of the audio-recording of what happened in the courtroom on the floor, and we submitted our own translation at that time, to which the Prosecution opposed in their response brief, and they say you cannot use that, you have to use an official translation. So we are in the process of obtaining this official translation. We've indicated that in our brief, simply to say that as soon as we have it, then we will be in a position to submit this official translation to the Appeals Chamber. So it is by no means a complaint. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So your reply is not fully complete?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Other than -- other than for this part of translation that we are -- that we will submit as soon as we get it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right. Good. Now, are there any other matters concerning the status of the appeals? Good. Then could we hear whether Mr. Hadzihasanovic has any concerns -- I'm sorry, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. At this point, the Defence of Mr. Kubura has no questions to raise before you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihasanovic, would you like to say whether the conditions of your detention are satisfactory? THE APPELLANT HADZIHASANOVIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I have nothing special to raise. The conditions, as well as my health, are quite well most of the time. Thank you, and thank you for having asked me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if there are no -- Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. There is one issue that we would like to alert the Appeals Chamber to on behalf of Mr. Hadzihasanovic, and that is that on behalf of Mr. Hadzihasanovic a request for early release. An application was filed before the President, and this application was filed on the 1st of March of this year. According to the applicable Practice Direction, we were under the understanding that a decision was to be rendered by the President seven days before the date of eligibility for early release. The date of eligibility according to us is 7 April, and we were hopefully expecting a decision before the Status Conference this morning. I have been in contact with the Office of the President, and they say the decision is in the making. We believe that it was important to mention this, so that it would be on the record of appeal that there is a pending matter before the President concerning the early release of Mr. Hadzihasanovic. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. You have referred to the Office of the President, and that means you are on home ground. It remains for me to remind you that the motion to which you refer is, I believe, a confidential document?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Indeed, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then shall we leave it this way, that we expect that the matter would be treated with the celerity it deserves, and that you will in due course hear from the Office of the President. Yes. Now, if there are no other matters, may we take the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, I'm reminded that it would be appropriate, would it not, to have the transcript redacted on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, I do not believe so because the application itself, although it was confidential, was actually given to the Appeals Chamber, and the Appeals Chamber -- it is on the record. So the Judges of the Appeals Chamber have received a copy of this application, and the fact that there is an application concerning early release is not a confidential matter. But there are issues inside the request itself that are confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right. Nothing in the motion has come out; all you have referred to is the existence of a motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That is correct, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So we'll leave it there then. Well, then maybe take the adjournment at this stage. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: adjourned at 8.27 a.m. 24
